On 15 January 2026, a violent jailbreak occurred at the Calabar Medium Security Correctional Center. During the escape, one of the inmates, Musa, attacked a correctional officer with a machete and attempted to seize the officer's firearm. In the ensuing struggle, another officer shot and killed Musa. On the same day, a group of armed robbers attacked a commercial bank in Calabar. While escaping, they opened fire on police officers and innocent bystanders. The police returned fire, killing one of the robbers, Emeka. A week later, following widespread protests over the increase in fuel prices, the Governor of Cross River State imposed a 24-hour curfew. Despite the curfew, a large crowd gathered and began looting government warehouses. After repeated warnings to disperse were ignored, the police fired live ammunition to disperse the crowd, resulting in the death of one protester, James. Eyewitnesses maintained that James was unarmed and was merely attempting to flee when he was shot. Meanwhile, Ibrahim was convicted of armed robbery by the High Court of Cross River State and sentenced to death. His appeal to the Court of Appeal and the Supreme Court was dismissed. He was subsequently executed by hanging pursuant to the Governor's death warrant. James' family and several human rights organizations instituted an action before the High Court, alleging that the killings of Musa, Emeka, James, and Ibrahim violated their constitutional right to life guaranteed under the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).

With reference to the relevant provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (where applicable), and decided cases:
1. Examine whether the killing of Musa by the correctional officer falls within any of the constitutional exceptions to the right to life.(5marks)
2. Critically assess whether the killing of James during the protest was constitutional. In your answer, discuss the constitutional requirement that only such force as is reasonably necessary may be used. (5marks).

The National Assembly enacted the National Social Welfare and Universal Healthcare Act, 2025, to implement Sections 16 and 17 of Chapter II of the Constitution. Under the Act, every Nigerian citizen is entitled to free primary healthcare and certain social welfare benefits. Following budget cuts, the Federal Government suspended the Act's implementation indefinitely. Aggrieved citizens instituted an action before the Federal High Court seeking an order compelling the Government to implement the Act. The Attorney-General of the Federation raised a preliminary objection, arguing that the provisions of Chapter II of the Constitution are non-justiciable by virtue of Section 6(6)(c).
Discuss the nature and Scope of fundamental rights under the 1999 Constitution (As amended)

A citizen is a native or naturalized individual who owes allegiance to a government and is entitled to governmental protection and to the exercise of civil rights. With recourse to relevant sections of the 1999 Constitution (As amended), elucidate on how to acquire a Nigerian citizenship.

The National Assembly recently enacted the National Environmental Sanitation Regulation Act, 2026, which established standards for environmental sanitation throughout Nigeria. Pursuant to the Act, every State House of Assembly was directed to enact corresponding laws within six months. The Cross River State House of Assembly, however, enacted the Cross River Environmental Management Law, 2026, introducing standards that differ substantially from those contained in the federal legislation. The Governor of Cross River State argues that environmental sanitation is primarily a state matter and that the State House of Assembly is constitutionally competent to legislate without primarily a state matter and that the State House of Assembly is constitutionally competent to legislate without regard to the federal law. The Attorney-General of the Federation contends that the federal law prevails and that the inconsistent provisions of the State Law are void. Meanwhile, members of the National Assembly have accused the President of unduly influencing the passage of the federal legislation by threatening to withhold assent from other pending Bills unless the Environmental Sanitation Bill was passed in its original form. Some commentators argue that this conduct undermines the constitutional doctrine of separation of powers.

As a Constitutional Law expert, advise the parties on the following:

(a) Examine the constitutional relationship between the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly under Section 4 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), highlighting the scope and limitations of their legislative powers. (10 marks)

(b) Explain the constitutional principle of "covering the field" and determine whether it applies to the above facts. (7and a half marks.)

(Support your answers with relevant constitutional provisions and decided cases.)

Following the creation of Okon Local Government Area by the Cross River State House of Assembly, disputes have arisen concerning its legal status and powers. The Legislative Council of Okon Local Government passed a Bye-law imposing sanitation levies, regulating markets, and licensing commercial motorcycle operators within the Local Government Area. The State Government subsequently directed the Local Government to suspend the Bye-law, arguing that the Council lacked constitutional authority to enact it. In addition, the Chairman of the Local Government complained that despite constitutional guarantees, the Local Government has been unable to discharge its constitutional responsibilities because the State Government controls its allocations from the Federation Account.

Advise the parties on the following issues:
(a) Discuss the legislative powers of a Local Government Legislative Council and examine the constitutional functions of Local Government Councils in Nigeria. (10 marks).
(b) Discuss the constitutional and statutory sources of finance available to Local Government Councils and the legal implications of undue interference with their finances.

(Support your answers with relevant constitutional provisions and judicial authorities.)(7and a half marks.

Chief Akintola Williams, a prominent politician, is facing corruption and money laundering charges initiated by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Fearing a conviction, Chief Akintola uses his political influence to lobby the newly appointed Attorney General (AG). The AG subsequently files a nolle prosequi to discontinue the criminal proceedings. The EFCC and HAMMER, a civil society group, object, arguing that the discontinuance is politically motivated, done in bad faith, and ignores the public interest. They approach the High Court seeking an order to set aside the AG's notice of discontinuance. Citing relevant sections of the Constitution and case law, determine the following issues:
1. Does the AG have the constitutional power to discontinue criminal proceedings initiated by other authorities? (7 and a half marks).
2. Can a court inquire into the motives or reasons behind the AG's exercise of the power of nolle prosequi? (5marks)
3. Assess the conflict between the AG's "unfettered" discretion and the constitutional mandate to have regard to
Nigeria Police Force in maintaining law and order in Nigeria. Clearly list and briefly explain the major functions (14 Marks).

The Constitution of a nation is the fons et origo, not only of the jurisprudence but also of the legal system of the nation. It is the beginning and the end of the legal system. In Greek, it is the alpha and omega. It is the barometer with which all statutes are measured. In line with the kingly position of the Constitution, all three branches of government are its servants, not in the sense of servitude or bondage, but in the sense of total obedience and loyalty to it. This is in recognition of the Supremacy of the Constitution above every statute, be it an act of the National Assembly or a law of the House of Assembly of a State.
Critically analyse this dictum vis-à-vis the doctrine of parliamentary supremacy while highlighting the advantages and disadvantages of parliamentary supremacy. (15 marks)

Since the amalgamation of the Northern and Southern protectorates of Nigeria under the Constitution of Sir (later on Lord) Lugard in 1914, the Nigerian constitutions have, at one time or another, exhibited the various characteristics of the world’s constitutions. Thus, the various Nigerian Constitutions have been classified as either written or unwritten, or, like the erudite Dr. Obot Essien added, non-written; rigid or flexible; federal, or monarchical; and presidential or parliamentary. Critically examine the various classifications, stating the plausibility or otherwise of a written constitution. (15marks.)

As a constitutional law student, you have been nominated to represent the University of Calabar in the public hearing for constitutional amendment. Make an intelligent overview of the constitutional development of Nigeria from the advent of British Rule up to the present. (12marks)
Highlight its features (5 1/2marks)

(I) Discuss the various types of coup d'etat in Nigeria (5marks)
(ii) Expatiate on the failed and successful coup plots during the military regime in Nigeria (5marks)
(iii) Discuss the distinction between military decrees and the Constitution. (7¹⁄₂ marks)

(I) Discuss the legal consequences of a change of government by extra-constitutional means (10marks)
(II) Explain the various types of decrees promulgated by the military junta during military government. (7¹⁄₂marks)
